did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 12 opens with a summary of Israel’s past conquests east of the Jordan, from the Arnon River to Mount Hermon and all the Arabah east of the Jordan.
Did you know? Sihon king of the Amorites is described as ruling from Heshbon over the territory stretching from the Arnon Valley to the Jabbok River, which was the border of the Ammonites.
Did you know? Og king of Bashan is described as ruling from two cities: Ashtaroth and Edrei.
Did you know? Og’s territory included Mount Hermon, Salecah, and all Bashan, as far as the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites, as well as half of Gilead.
Did you know? Moses and the Israelites defeated Sihon and Og, and Moses gave their land as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

Did you know? After summarizing the conquests east of the Jordan, the chapter turns to the kings whom Joshua and the Israelites defeated west of the Jordan, from Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir.
Did you know? The verse describes a variety of regions in the land—the hill country, lowlands, Arabah, slopes, wilderness, and Negev—and mentions the peoples who had previously lived in them.
Did you know? The list of kings west of the Jordan begins with the king of Jericho and the king of Ai, noting that each had a separate city and kingdom in the list.
Did you know? Among the northern kings mentioned in the chapter are the kings of Madon, Hazor, Shimron-meron, and Achshaph.
Did you know? The chapter ends with a clear numerical summary: Joshua listed a total of thirty-one kings of the land.
